title: Eufy's Floodlight Cam Hits Record Low Price—Here's Why It's a Game-Changer
summary: If you've ever squinted at a grainy nighttime video of a porch pirate, you'll appreciate what the Eufy E340 Floodlight Camera brings to the table. And right now, it's at the lowest price I've ever seen—making it a Prime Day deal worth pouncing on. What sets this camera apart? First, the floodlights. While most security cameras offer a weak spotlight, the E340 packs two adjustable LED panels that blast 2,000 lumens—enough to turn a pitch-black driveway into a well-lit stage. You can tweak brightness and angle in the app, so you're not blinding the neighbors. But the real magic is the dual-lens system. A 3K wide-angle lens captures the scene, while a 2K telephoto lens with 8X zoom grabs details like faces or license plates up to 50 feet away. And because the floodlights are on, you get color footage at night—no murky black-and-white blobs. The camera pans 360 degrees and tilts 120 degrees, and its AI tracking automatically follows a person, pet, or vehicle, then returns to a preset position. You can set patrol points to cover a wide area. I've been testing one for two years, and it's impressively accurate—though it occasionally mistakes my large cat for a human. The Eufy ecosystem's killer feature is local storage. Skip the monthly cloud fees: just insert a microSD card up to 128GB, or connect to a HomeBase 3 (sold separately). Alerts are swift, with on-device AI distinguishing between people, pets, and cars. There's also two-way audio, a 95-decibel siren, and customizable activity zones. The catch? It requires a wired power connection, so you'll need an outlet nearby or an electrician's help. But for a one-time purchase that delivers pro-level surveillance without a subscription, this deal is hard to beat.

background_read: A "porch pirate" is a thief who steals packages left at front doors — a common problem in many neighborhoods, making security cameras popular.
Floodlight cameras combine bright lights with video surveillance; traditional models often need a monthly cloud subscription to store footage.
Eufy is a smart home brand owned by Anker, known for devices that prioritize local data storage over paid cloud plans.
Amazon's Prime Day is a major annual sale event where electronics often see steep discounts, so deals like this draw a lot of attention.

perspectives.description: At its lowest price, this camera delivers professional-grade security without a subscription. It empowers homeowners to deter porch pirates and monitor property with clear, color night footage.

The wired power requirement can be a dealbreaker for renters or those without an outdoor outlet. Some users might also worry about false AI identifications or the need to buy a separate HomeBase for extended storage.

perspectives.perspective: Neutral / analytical – shifting security camera market
perspectives.description: As more brands offer local storage and on-device AI, consumers are moving away from monthly cloud fees. Eufy's model challenges subscription-based competitors, but the long-term reliability and software support of such ecosystems remain a question.

If local-storage cameras become the norm, subscription-dependent companies may be forced to lower prices or offer free tiers. For individuals, the shift means a one-time purchase can provide years of surveillance, making safe neighborhoods less dependent on ongoing payments.
